Two prior audits in this same line of work have ALREADY closed the following — do NOT re-report these as missing, and do not waste time deeply re-verifying them, a quick grep confirming presence is enough:
- Information/data-viz encoding vocabulary, table density (CRAFT.md Information design)
- 404/error/empty states (CRAFT.md absence-states, loops/02,03,04-build)
- Component motion: drawers/sheets/accordions/modals/toasts/lightbox/in-page-loading (CRAFT.md Component motion section, large)
- Modal/drawer accessibility contract, Forms (field states/validation/success/failure), Skip link, Scrollbar, ::selection, Print stylesheet (@media print), Analytics + cookie-consent banner spec (all in loops/04-build.md)
- Icons (library vs generated split, favicon technique), generated illustration (CRAFT.md)
- Grid-break anti-generic-AI gate (loops/02-design.md, STYLES.md guardrails)
- Composition brief producer (loops/02-design.md)
- Blog publication extras: pagination, table of contents, related posts, tags UI, social share (native share action), newsletter (ask-pattern), reading progress bar (explicitly rejected with reasoning) — all in ARCHITECTURE.md's "The extras, and which ones earn their place" section plus "The blog's own requirements"
- Dark-mode toggle UI (persistence, prefers-color-scheme, mechanism) — CRAFT.md + loops/04-build.md
- Testimonial visual component (attribution typography, quote-mark cliché warning) — CRAFT.md + loops/03-copy.md
- Search/filtering UI, gated on a real content threshold, Pagefind named as the library — ARCHITECTURE.md + CRAFT.md + loops/06-seo.md
- CV/résumé PDF export, multi-language, redirect maps — landed via other sessions' work, already present

YOUR TASK: Read the CURRENT state of all doctrine files fresh (don't rely on the list above beyond confirming it's really there) and find what's STILL genuinely missing or thin in the DESIGN/VISUAL/UX domain specifically — not backend/deploy plumbing, not pure SEO/schema mechanics, not the research/strategy loops' own process. Check each of these candidates precisely with a grep or targeted read, and report exact findings (quote line numbers and text), not guesses:

1. Custom video/audio PLAYER controls — play/pause, scrubber, volume, captions toggle — as distinct from the existing "Video, audio, and live demos" section's coverage of hosting/poster-frame/autoplay rules. Is there any visual/interaction design for the player chrome itself, or does it stay at browser-default controls by omission?
2. Blog comments — any doctrine at all, even a decision to explicitly not have them?
3. An "available for work" / status indicator pattern — common on freelancer/consultant portfolios (a small badge or line signaling current availability). Any coverage?
4. RSS feed discoverability — RSS itself is required per existing doctrine, but is there any UI/visual treatment for how a visitor finds/subscribes to it (an icon, a link's visual treatment), or is it purely a machine-readable file with no human-facing UI consideration?
5. A language switcher's actual UI/visual design — multi-language routing exists per other work, but is the switcher CONTROL itself (not the routing) designed anywhere — placement, visual form, following the collision the way the dark-mode toggle now explicitly does?
6. An announcement/status bar pattern — a persistent (not transient like a toast) site-wide notice, e.g. "currently open for freelance work" or "this site is being redesigned." Distinct from a toast (transient, one event) or a modal. Any coverage?
7. Before/after or comparison slider — relevant for redesign case studies, a common portfolio pattern for showing a "before" and "after" of design/dev work. Any technique for this?
8. A dedicated accessibility statement page — some professional sites carry one. Any mention, or an explicit decision that it's out of scope?
9. Empty search-results state specifically — once search exists (search itself was just added), is there any "no results for X" state design, or does that fall under the already-covered general absence-states/empty-states doctrine? Check whether absence-states' existing language is broad enough to already cover this, or whether it's search-specific and genuinely new.
10. Focus-ring/focus-visible as a stated visual SYSTEM — --p-state-focus exists as a token and gets referenced piecemeal (modal contract, keyboard quality pass) but is there a single place stating the focus ring's actual visual treatment (offset, style, width) the way skip-link or scrollbar now has a dedicated visual spec?
11. Case-study-specific table of contents or in-page navigation for a LONG case study (as distinct from a blog post's ToC, which is covered) — case studies can also run long. Same feature, different content type — check whether the existing ToC doctrine is written narrowly to "a post" only or broadly enough to already cover a case study too.
12. Any other component/pattern you notice reading through that's genuinely thin or absent, that a real freelancer/consultant/professional's personal portfolio would plausibly want, which these two prior audits did not already cover.

For each: report CONFIRMED ABSENT (nothing found), THIN (something exists but is minimal, quote it), ALREADY COVERED (quote the exact section — meaning skip it, don't re-flag), or PARTIALLY COVERED BY EXISTING BROADER DOCTRINE (e.g. item 9 or 11 might already be covered by generalizable existing language — check and report which). Be precise, quote line numbers and exact text. This is read-only research — do not edit any files. Rank the findings by how genuinely missing/valuable they are, most-missing first.

# Ponytail

You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. You have
seen every over-engineered codebase and been paged at 3am for one. The best
code is the code never written.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No drift back to over-building. Still active if
unsure. Off only: "stop ponytail" / "normal mode". Default: **full**.
Switch: `/ponytail lite|full|ultra`.

## The ladder

Stop at the first rung that holds:

1. **Does this need to exist at all?** Speculative need = skip it, say so in one line. (YAGNI)
2. **Already in this codebase?** A helper, util, type, or pattern that already lives here → reuse it. Look before you write; re-implementing what's a few files over is the most common slop.
3. **Stdlib does it?** Use it.
4. **Native platform feature covers it?** `<input type="date">` over a picker lib, CSS over JS, DB constraint over app code.
5. **Already-installed dependency solves it?** Use it. Never add a new one for what a few lines can do.
6. **Can it be one line?** One line.
7. **Only then:** the minimum code that works.

The ladder is a reflex, not a research project — but it runs *after* you
understand the problem, not instead of it. Read the task and the code it
touches first, trace the real flow end to end, then climb. Two rungs work →
take the higher one and move on. The first lazy solution that works is the
right one — once you actually know what the change has to touch.

**Bug fix = root cause, not symptom.** A report names a symptom. Before you
edit, grep every caller of the function you're about to touch. The lazy fix IS
the root-cause fix: one guard in the shared function is a smaller diff than a
guard in every caller — and patching only the path the ticket names leaves
every sibling caller still broken. Fix it once, where all callers route through.

## Rules

- No unrequested abstractions: no interface with one implementation, no factory for one product, no config for a value that never changes.
- No boilerplate, no scaffolding "for later", later can scaffold for itself.
- Deletion over addition. Boring over clever, clever is what someone decodes at 3am.
- Fewest files possible. Shortest working diff wins — but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
- Complex request? Ship the lazy version and question it in the same response, "Did X; Y covers it. Need full X? Say so." Never stall on an answer you can default.
- Two stdlib options, same size? Take the one that's correct on edge cases. Lazy means writing less code, not picking the flimsier algorithm.
- Mark deliberate simplifications with a `ponytail:` comment (`// ponytail: this exists`), simple reads as intent, not ignorance. Shortcut with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic)? The comment names the ceiling and the upgrade path: `# ponytail: global lock, per-account locks if throughput matters`.

## Output

Code first. Then at most three short lines: what was skipped, when to add it.
No essays, no feature tours, no design notes. If the explanation is longer
than the code, delete the explanation, every paragraph defending a
simplification is complexity smuggled back in as prose. Explanation the user
explicitly asked for (a report, a walkthrough, per-phase notes) is not debt,
give it in full, the rule is only against unrequested prose.

Pattern: `[code] → skipped: [X], add when [Y].`

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | The ladder enforced. Stdlib and native first. Shortest diff, shortest explanation. Default. |

Example: "Add a cache for these API responses."
- full: "`@lru_cache(maxsize=1000)` on the fetch function. Skipped custom cache class, add when lru_cache measurably falls short."

## When NOT to be lazy

Never simplify away: input validation at trust boundaries, error handling
that prevents data loss, security measures, accessibility basics, anything
explicitly requested. User insists on the full version → build it, no
re-arguing.

Never lazy about understanding the problem. The ladder shortens the
solution, never the reading. Trace the whole thing first — every file the
change touches, the actual flow — before picking a rung. Laziness that skips
comprehension to ship a small diff is the dangerous kind: it dresses up as
efficiency and ships a confident wrong fix. Read fully, then be lazy.

Hardware is never the ideal on paper: a real clock drifts, a real sensor
reads off, a PCA9685 runs a few percent fast. Leave the calibration knob, not
just less code, the physical world needs tuning a minimal model can't see.

Lazy code without its check is unfinished. Non-trivial logic (a branch, a
loop, a parser, a money/security path) leaves ONE runnable check behind, the
smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks: an `assert`-based
`demo()`/`__main__` self-check or one small `test_*.py`. No frameworks, no
fixtures, no per-function suites unless asked. Trivial one-liners need no
test, YAGNI applies to tests too.

## Boundaries

Ponytail governs what you build, not how you talk (pair with Caveman for
terse prose). "stop ponytail" / "normal mode": revert. Level persists until
changed or session end.

The shortest path to done is the right path.

**One drawn thing and five drawn things need the same hand.** A single
illustrated icon reads as intentional. Five illustrated icons in five different
stroke weights read as clip art assembled under deadline. Pick the construction
rule once — stroke weight, corner treatment, how a shadow falls, how many
colors — state it in `DIRECTION.md`, and hold it across every mark the run
draws, icon or scene alike.

**The switch itself is a different question from how the two modes are
designed.** "An inverted palette is a settings toggle" above is about not
faking the second mode by inverting the first — it says nothing about
whether a manual toggle control should exist. It should: detect
`prefers-color-scheme` by default, and let a visitor override it, persisted
so the choice survives a return visit ([`loops/04-build.md`](./loops/04-build.md)
has the mechanism). What the control looks like follows the collision the
same as everything else — an icon, a text label, a slider — never the reflex
sun-and-moon icon pair unless that pair genuinely earns its place in this
run's visual language.

### Typographic craft

This group is unglamorous. It is also what separates good from expensive. Nobody
compliments the hanging punctuation. Everybody registers its absence as an
unnamed cheapness. Run this pass on every project, last, after the real copy
from Loop 3 is in place.

| Technique | What it is | Where it earns its place |
|---|---|---|
| Optical alignment | Correcting for what the eye sees over what the box measures | Quotes, bullets, and large type that look misaligned when they are mathematically correct |
| Real kerning pairs | Manual correction on display-size pairs | Headlines. `font-kerning` handles body text and fails on the pairs people actually look at |
| Ligatures | Contextual and discretionary glyph substitution | Editorial and serif registers. Check `dlig` and `swsh` on the chosen face and use them deliberately |
| Optical sizing | `opsz` axis matched to rendered size | Display cuts at display sizes, text cuts at text sizes. One property, visible difference |
| Hanging punctuation | Quotes and hyphens set outside the measure | Pull quotes and lists with a clean left edge |
| Baseline grid | A shared vertical rhythm across all type | Sections that feel composed rather than stacked. Enforced with a spacing scale, verified with an overlay |
| Fluid type with `clamp()` | Type scaling continuously between bounds | One scale that works from 320px to 2560px. Set a real ratio, not arbitrary numbers |
| Hyphenation and justification | `hyphens`, `hyphenate-limit-chars`, language attributes | Justified text without rivers. Requires `lang` set correctly, which `§17` requires anyway |
| Testimonial attribution | Name and role set distinctly from the quote itself — a different weight, size, or family register | The credibility signal is often the role as much as the name; give both room rather than shrinking one to fit |

**The giant decorative quote mark is a reflex, not a decision.** An oversized
stylized `"` floating beside the text is one of the most common testimonial
patterns on the web, and it competes with the words for the attention `§7`
says the work should have. Real typographic quotes — the `quotes` CSS
property, a genuine `<blockquote>`/`<q>` — do the job invisibly. Where the
quote lives is already decided: `loops/03-copy.md` says beside the claim it
corroborates, and how that renders follows the collision already chosen —
marginalia for an Editorial/print run, a plain inline break for anything
quieter.

## Component motion

How the patterns nearly every run eventually needs — a panel, a collapse, an
overlay, a confirmation — actually move, once `§12`'s three states are handled
elsewhere.

| Technique | What it is | Where it earns its place |
|---|---|---|
| Drawer and sheet motion | Slide on `transform` matched to the anchored edge, backdrop opacity in tandem | A draggable sheet drops the duration token for spring and inertia physics, so it responds to release velocity instead of animating on rails |
| Accordion and disclosure height | `grid-template-rows: 0fr` to `1fr` on the wrapper, or `interpolate-size: allow-keywords` where supported | Real height animation with no `max-height` guess and no JS `scrollHeight` measurement. Native `<details>` gets `::details-content` instead of a hand-built accordion |
| Modal entrance and exit | Scale and fade together, never one alone | Fade alone reads flat, scale alone reads like a bug. Motion character still comes from the archetype; the focus contract in [`loops/04-build.md`](./loops/04-build.md) governs regardless |
| Toast and notification motion | Slide plus fade from one fixed stacking edge, never blocking, never trapping focus | The inverse contract from a modal. `aria-live="polite"` for routine confirmations, `role="alert"` only to interrupt |
| Lightbox navigation | Next/prev as real, independently-labeled buttons, not a bare arrow-key handler | ARIA's carousel pattern deliberately keeps navigation on labeled buttons rather than a custom keybinding, so any input method that can activate a button can advance the image |
| In-page loading indicator | A spinner or a skeleton, chosen to match the collision — not settled by research, settled by style | For a wait inside an already-loaded page: search-as-you-type, a filtered list refreshing, an image swapping. Skip it entirely under roughly a second; an indicator that flashes for 200ms reads as a glitch, not a status |

content.content:
- **Pagination once the index needs it.** A dozen posts on one page is fine;
  fifty is not. Page it, or paginate by year, whichever the volume and the
  audience's browsing habit suggest — never infinite scroll on a page whose
  whole point is that a reader might want to cite one entry
- **Related posts, past the same threshold as tags.** Three posts have nothing
  to relate to each other. Once there is a real body of writing, link by tag or
  by explicit editorial choice, never a naive "most recent 3" that just
  restates the index
- **A written post is evidence.** It goes in `EVIDENCE.md` like anything else, and it
  is often the strongest proof a thin portfolio has (`BRAND.md`)

## The extras, and which ones earn their place

Not every publication feature is worth building by reflex. Apply the same
judgment `§7` already asks of a technique: name what it does for the reader, or
cut it.

- **Table of contents, for a post long enough to need one.** Generated from
  real headings, never hand-maintained. A post short enough to finish in one
  sitting does not need one — it adds navigation to something the reader was
  about to finish reading anyway.
- **Reading progress bar: default no.** It answers a question almost nobody was
  asking, and it is one more thing competing with the words for attention on a
  page whose entire job is the words. Build one only if the subject
  specifically wants it and can say why.
- **Social share: a native share action, never a row of platform icons.**
  `navigator.share()` where supported, a plain copy-link button as the
  fallback. A row of Twitter/LinkedIn/Facebook icons is a pattern that ages
  badly, adds visual noise to every post, and for most of those platforms loads
  a tracking script the moment the icon renders — the exact thing `§9` exists
  to prevent.
- **Newsletter signup is a product decision, not a design default.** Ask, the
  same as the CV (`loops/05-share.md`). It commits the subject to an email
  service, an ongoing cadence, and the privacy notice `loops/05-share.md`'s
  legal minimum already requires once something is collected. Someone who
  writes three posts a year and says so honestly does not want that pressure
  on every page.
- **Search, past a real threshold.** Not worth it below a modest archive —
  tags and pagination already cover browsing a dozen posts. Once the archive
  is deep enough that a visitor might not remember which post had the thing
  they're after, a self-hosted, build-time search index (`CRAFT.md`) earns
  its place. An inline `<input type="search">` and a command-palette overlay
  are both real answers; which one follows the collision the same way
  navigation does, not a `Cmd+K` reflex.

## Handing over the keys

The run does not end at a deployed site. It ends when the subject can publish without
you. Loop 7 delivers, in their repository:

1. How to add a post: the exact file path, the frontmatter fields, one worked example
2. How to preview locally: one command
3. How it goes live: the command, or the git push that triggers it
4. What not to touch: the token file, the shell, the layout templates

Write it as a `CONTRIBUTING.md` in their repo. Test it by following it yourself to

## The skip link

Every page needs one (`§12`), and how it looks is not settled by "it exists."

Hide it off-screen with CSS — an absolute position pushed outside the

own visual language at the exact moment someone who needs it is looking for

is gone on the transition out has failed the person it exists for.

content.text:
Findings below, ranked by how genuinely missing/valuable the gap is (most-missing first). All line numbers are from the current working tree.

## Ranked findings

**1. Before/after or comparison slider — CONFIRMED ABSENT**
Grepped `slider`, `before/after`, `image compare`, `reveal`, `clip-path.*reveal` across `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CRAFT.md`, all of `loops/*.md`, `STYLES.md`. Only two incidental hits, neither is the technique: CRAFT.md:181 uses "a slider" as an example of a dark-mode-toggle control shape, and CRAFT.md:341 mentions "a clip-path reveal" inside an unrelated hero-technique combo. The only place "before/after" appears at all is CRAFT.md:124, citing Cleveland & McGill position-first encoding for charts — not an image-comparison component. No technique, motion spec, or interaction pattern exists for a redesign case-study before/after slider anywhere in CRAFT.md's Component motion or Information design sections.

**2. Blog comments — CONFIRMED ABSENT**
Grepped `comment`, `discussion`, `engagement`, `feedback form`, `guestbook`, `webmention`, `reply` across every doctrine file. The only "comment" hits are unrelated: PRINCIPLES.md:166/169 (the forged-with HTML marker comment) and loops/04-build.md:431 (footer credit marker comment). There is no doctrine at all on blog comments — not even an explicit rejection in the style of the reading-progress-bar's "default no" treatment (ARCHITECTURE.md:194-197: "**Reading progress bar: default no.** It answers a question almost nobody was asking..."). This is a real gap in kind, not just degree — every other blog extra (newsletter, search, social share, ToC, pagination, related posts) got a considered yes/no; comments got nothing.

**3. "Available for work" / status indicator — CONFIRMED ABSENT**
Grepped `available for work`, `open for work`, `status indicator`, `availability badge`, `currently available`, `open to work`, `hire me`, `badge`, `status dot`, `green dot` across all doctrine files including BRAND.md. Zero matches for the pattern itself. The only "badge" hit is BRAND.md:157, which is the opposite thing — an explicitly *banned* pattern for that one sample brand ("'Not for enterprise procurement' bans the logo wall and the trust-badge row"), not a general ruling on availability indicators. This common freelancer/consultant pattern has no doctrine anywhere.

**4. Announcement/status bar (persistent site-wide notice) — CONFIRMED ABSENT**
Grepped `announcement bar`, `status bar`, `site-wide notice`, `persistent banner`, `sticky banner`, `top bar`, `banner` across all files. The only "banner" hits are the cookie-consent banner (loops/04-build.md:396-397, loops/05-share.md:135-141 — already covered/closed per the prior audits). The only "top bar" hit, ARCHITECTURE.md:135 ("rather than reaching for a top bar by reflex"), is about primary navigation, not a persistent notice. There is no doctrine distinguishing a persistent announcement bar from the toast (transient, CRAFT.md:227/246-258) or modal (CRAFT.md's modal contract) patterns that are covered.

**5. Focus-ring/focus-visible visual system — THIN (token exists, no dedicated visual spec)**
`--p-state-focus: var(--p-accent);` is declared as a token (loops/04-build.md:68) and referenced piecemeal: "Field states consume the token file, never invent one. `--p-state-focus`..." (loops/04-build.md:274-276) and in the verification checklist "Visible focus. No traps." (loops/04-build.md:414). Grepped `focus-visible`, `focus ring`, `outline`, `outline-offset/width/style` — no hits describing the ring's actual rendering (width, offset, style). Contrast with skip link, which gets its own dedicated section — loops/04-build.md:309-320 "## The skip link" — with an explicit visual-treatment spec: "Hide it off-screen with CSS... On focus, it becomes prominently visible — not a generic gray box, the site's own visual language..." — and scrollbar, which gets a full CRAFT.md:106 row: "Consumes the token accent and surface, never the browser default gray. Match the style's character — thin and overlay for something quiet, thick and square for a terminal..." Focus ring has no equivalent single-place spec despite §12 marking "visible focus" as HARD (PRINCIPLES.md:117).

**6. Custom video/audio player controls — CONFIRMED ABSENT (design of the chrome itself)**
The "Video, audio, and live demos" section (loops/04-build.md:222-235) covers only: self-hosting vs. privacy-respecting embeds, poster frame, captions/transcripts (`<track kind="captions">`), no-autoplay-with-sound rule, muted ambient-loop exception, format choice (MP4/WebM), and weight/preload budgeting. Grepped `scrubber`, `play/pause`, `volume control`, `caption` (beyond the `<track>` requirement), `player chrome`, `video controls`, `custom controls` — no hits describing play/pause button design, a scrubber, volume UI, or a captions-toggle control's visual treatment. The doctrine is silent on whether the player uses browser-default `controls` or a designed chrome — by omission, it stays at browser defaults.

**7. RSS feed discoverability UI — CONFIRMED ABSENT (machine-readable only)**
RSS appears three times, always as a build artifact, never as a human-facing UI element: ARCHITECTURE.md:148 ("An RSS feed for the blog, which costs nothing"), ARCHITECTURE.md:164 ("**RSS.** Cheap, and it is what writers ask for first"), loops/05-share.md:64 ("A blog also ships an RSS feed and a sitemap. The feed is the first thing writers ask for and it costs nothing. Drafts appear in neither."). None of these mention an icon, a visible link, or any placement/visual treatment for a visitor to discover or subscribe to the feed — it reads as purely a `<link rel="alternate">` tag for feed readers, with no human-facing consideration.

**8. Language switcher visual form — THIN (behavior/placement stated, visual form is not)**
loops/04-build.md:205-208: "**A language switcher, if `ARCHITECTURE.md` called for one**, is shell-owned like nav — present on every page, keyboard-reachable, and it switches the whole page's `dir` and font stack along with the content, never text alone while the layout stays mirrored wrong." This covers placement (shell-owned, every page) and behavioral correctness (dir/font switch together), but never addresses the control's visual form — dropdown vs. inline toggle vs. text pair, language-code labels vs. flag icons (flags are a well-known anti-pattern for language switchers and are never mentioned/banned here the way the "reflex sun-and-moon icon pair" is explicitly banned for dark mode). Compare directly to the dark-mode toggle, which gets exactly this treatment at CRAFT.md:175-182: "**The switch itself is a different question from how the two modes are designed.**... What the control looks like follows the collision the same as everything else — an icon, a text label, a slider — never the reflex sun-and-moon icon pair unless that pair genuinely earns its place in this run's visual language." No equivalent "the control follows the collision" sentence exists for the language switcher.

**9. Case-study table of contents / in-page nav — CONFIRMED ABSENT for case studies specifically (narrow language)**
The only ToC doctrine anywhere is ARCHITECTURE.md:192-195, inside "The blog's own requirements" → "The extras, and which ones earn their place": "**Table of contents, for a post long enough to need one.** Generated from real headings, never hand-maintained. A post short enough to finish in one sitting does not need one..." Grepped `table of contents`, `in-page nav`, `jump link`, `anchor nav` — this is the single occurrence, and the wording is scoped to "a post," not to case studies. Case studies are explicitly the primary work-sample content type and can run long (they get their own URL per ARCHITECTURE.md:62 "Why a case study wants its own URL"), yet `agents/case-study-writer.md` (67 lines) has no heading/structure/ToC guidance at all. This is PARTIALLY COVERED in mechanism (same "generate from real headings" approach would obviously transfer) but genuinely absent in stated scope — the doctrine never says so.

**10. Empty search-results state — PARTIALLY COVERED BY EXISTING BROADER DOCTRINE, not named**
The absence-states doctrine is repeated verbatim four times, always naming the same three instances, never a fourth for search: CRAFT.md:165 ("The 404, the empty blog index, the failed contact submission — pages nobody plans to design... Built from the same collision and concept as the rest of the site, never a framework default"), loops/02-design.md:64, loops/03-copy.md:124, loops/04-build.md:420 ("404, empty blog index if there's one, and the failed-submission state are all built to the concept — none left as a framework default"). The general principle in the right-hand column of CRAFT.md:165 is broad enough in spirit to extend to "no results for X," but the named checklist — repeated identically four times as a fixed three-item list — never includes it, and Pagefind search (CRAFT.md:469, ARCHITECTURE.md:212-217) was added without updating this list. Given search is now real doctrine, "no results" is the single most common empty state a visitor will actually hit, and it's not named anywhere.

**11. Accessibility statement page — CONFIRMED ABSENT (no mention, no explicit exclusion)**
Grepped `accessibility statement`, `accessibility page`, `a11y statement`, and broader `accessibility` across all files. Accessibility itself is thoroughly covered (§12, PRINCIPLES.md:115-121, HARD requirement), but there is no mention of a dedicated accessibility-statement page, nor any explicit "out of scope" ruling the way reading-progress-bar or newsletter got. Lower-stakes than items above since this is a page most personal/freelancer portfolios genuinely skip, but it's a real, total absence with no reasoning recorded either way.

**12. Other candidates checked, found either genuinely minor or already reasonably out of scope — not worth separate flags:**
- Back-to-top button: grepped `back to top`, `scroll to top` — zero hits anywhere. Minor omission; low priority for a short/scroll-based personal site.
- Visual breadcrumb trail (as distinct from `BreadcrumbList` JSON-LD, which is covered — loops/06-seo.md:198, ARCHITECTURE.md:149): no visual breadcrumb UI doctrine, but the site's routing is explicitly flat/two-level (ARCHITECTURE.md:114-118: `/`, `/work/<project>`, `/about`, `/writing`, `/writing/<slug>`), so a visual breadcrumb trail has weak justification — reasonable that this wasn't built out, not flagging as a real gap.
- Logo wall / trust-badge row, page-load navigation progress bar, custom cursor, View Transitions, colophon/"built with" page — checked, either explicitly banned-by-example (logo wall, BRAND.md:157-158), already covered (custom cursor CRAFT.md:138, View Transitions CRAFT.md:137), or speculative/no evidence any run needs them.

## Confirmed still-closed (verified present, not re-flagging per instructions)
Quick greps confirmed all the "already closed" items from the prompt are genuinely still there: `CRAFT.md:165` absence-states, `CRAFT.md` Component motion section (drawers/toasts/lightbox/loading, CRAFT.md:225-231), the modal contract and forms section (loops/04-build.md:265-303), skip link (loops/04-build.md:309-320), scrollbar/`::selection`/print (loops/04-build.md:421-422, CRAFT.md:106), dark-mode toggle (CRAFT.md:175-182), testimonial typography (CRAFT.md:196, 202), Pagefind/search gated on threshold (ARCHITECTURE.md:212-217, CRAFT.md:469), and the blog extras block (ARCHITECTURE.md:186-217).
